statement: You are given an array intervals, where intervals[i] = [start, end] describes a closed range with start ≤ end. The intervals may come in any order.

Two intervals overlap if they share at least one point, including when one ends exactly where the other starts. Merge every group of overlapping intervals into a single interval that covers the whole group.
Return the merged intervals, which no longer overlap, ordered by start.

examples.explanation: [1, 3] and [2, 6] overlap and merge into [1, 6]. [8, 10] and [15, 18] touch nothing else.
After sorting by start, [2, 3] lies inside [1, 4], and [4, 5] touches it at 4, so all three become [1, 5]. [10, 12] stays separate.
